title: The radial profile of dust grain size in the protoplanetary disc of DS Tau
question: What is the radial profile of dust grain size in the protoplanetary disk of DS Tau, and how does it correlate with disk substructures?

what.value: Optical to millimeter SED photometry of DS Tau (Table 1)

evidence.quote: Table 1 lists the measured flux densities of DS Tau, and the data points cover a broad range of wavelength from the optical to millimeter.

what.value: ALMA Band 6 and Band 3 continuum images and flux densities

evidence.quote: Details of the ALMA observations and data reduction can be found in (cite: 2018ApJ...869...17L; 2020ApJ...898...36L).

what.value: Gap location and width (32 or 33 AU and 27 AU)

evidence.quote: The gap location and width are denoted as $R_{\mathrm {gap}}$ and $\sigma$, and are set to 32 AU and 27 AU according to (cite: 2018ApJ...869...17L).

what.value: Spectral type (M0.4) and effective temperature (3800 K / 3792 K) of DS Tau

evidence.quote: The central star has a spectral type of M0.4 and an effective temperature of 3800 K (cite: 2014ApJ...786...97H).
Our research target, DS Tau, is an M0.4 young star (cite: 2014ApJ...786...97H) in the Taurus star-forming region at a distance of 158 pc (cite: 2021A&A...649A...1G).

what.value: Accretion luminosity of DS Tau (0.05 L_odot)

evidence.quote: (cite: 2018ApJ...868...28F) calculated the accretion luminosity to be $0.05\,\mathrm\,L_{\odot}$, which is only 7% of the blackbody luminosity of the central star.

recipe.goal: Extract radial intensity profiles and spectral index profile from ALMA images
recipe.method: Convolve Band 3 and Band 6 ALMA images to a common beam of [0.13'', 0.09''], extract radial intensity profiles by azimuthal averaging on concentric ellipses defined by disk inclination and position angle, and compute the spectral index alpha_mm(R).
key_parameters: Inclination i = 67.58 deg, Position angle = 159.62 deg
assumptions: Absolute flux calibration uncertainty (~10%) is neglected in main modeling

recipe.goal: Fit the SED to determine representative disk geometry parameters
recipe.method: Run a grid of self-consistent two-layer flared disk radiative transfer models in RADMC-3D with isotropic scattering and constant midplane maximum grain size, minimizing chi^2_SED over the two ALMA wavelengths (and checking against the full SED) to find best-fit H_100 and beta.
key_parameters: H_100 in [5, 10] AU (6 grid points); beta in [1.00, 1.15] (4 grid points); gamma in [0.3, 1.5] (7 grid points); M_dust in [10^-7, 10^-2] M_odot (11 grid points); a_max^mid in [10^3, 10^5] um (5 grid points)
Fixed parameters: M_* = 0.58 M_odot, T_eff = 3792 K, L_* = 0.7 L_odot, R_in = 0.1 AU, R_out = 80 AU, R_gap = 33 AU, sigma = 27 AU, eta = 0.99, H_ratio = 0.2, D = 158 pc
assumptions: 85% of total dust mass in midplane, 15% in surface layer; surface layer a_max = 1 um, a_min = 0.01 um, size distribution slope p = 3.5

DSHARP homogeneous sphere dust composition (20% water ice, 32% astronomical silicates, 8% troilite, 40% refractory organics; rho_dust = 1.675 g cm^-3) with Bruggeman and Mie theory and isotropic scattering

recipe.goal: Iteratively reconstruct the dust surface density profile Sigma(R) and fit the radial maximum grain size profile a_max^mid(R)
recipe.method: Divide the disk midplane (out to 80 AU) into 32 radial bins of width 2.5 AU. Initialize a_max^mid(R) with a power law (a_max0 = 1000 um, b = 6 at R0 = 40 AU) and fix a_max^mid = 10 cm for R < 20 AU. Sequentially from inner to outer bins, perform a dense logarithmic grid search of a_max^mid to fit the observed spectral index alpha_mm(R). For every trial model, iteratively adjust Sigma(R) from scratch using the 2.9 mm observed-to-model radial intensity ratio until convergence (<5% change, ~12 iterations). Estimate uncertainties using 17 logarithmically spaced models in [log(a_best)-0.4, log(a_best)+0.4] per bin weighted by 1/chi^2.
key_parameters: 32 radial bins of width 2.5 AU; fixed H_100 = 7 AU, beta = 1.05; initial Sigma(R) with gamma = 0.5
Initial power-law search: R_0 = 40 AU, a_max0 in [100, 10000 um], b in [1, 8]; best initial power law a_max0 = 1000 um, b = 6; fixed a_max^mid = 10 cm for R < 20 AU
Convergence threshold: < 5% surface density change at any radius (~ 12 iterations); 17 models per bin for uncertainty
assumptions: Image-plane fitting is valid because uv sampling is similar between bands and MRS (~1.8'' and ~2.6'') is much larger than disk outer radius (~0.5'')

recipe.goal: Estimate depleted dust mass in the gap and evaluate Toomre Q gravitational stability
recipe.method: Interpolate a smooth power-law dust surface density between R = 6 AU and R = 60 AU, integrate to find the pre-depletion dust mass, and subtract the best-fit dust mass. Compute the radial Toomre Q parameter from the midplane temperature and scaled gas surface density.
assumptions: Uniform gas-to-dust mass ratio of 30 (and tested < 10 in the ring)
